openai.feedback:
- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/group_g4.py:43
- Finding: The ID pattern has no trailing boundary, so `Fixes trg-aaaaaaaa0` is parsed as closing `trg-aaaaaaaa`. If that eight-digit card exists and is open, G4 reports a false finding; otherwise it emits an incorrect unknown-ID line. This violates the grammar requiring an eight-hex-digit ID.
- Suggestion: Add a trailing identifier boundary to `_ID` so longer identifiers cannot match a valid prefix. Add negative fixtures for nine-digit IDs and IDs followed by identifier characters, including within closing lists.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The diff appears to cover all three acceptance criteria, but the token parser needs this correction before shipping.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/test_audit_group_g4_close_tokens.py:123-126 (`test_registered_under_group_g`)
  Finding: The test only asserts `"G" in audit_detector._GROUPS`. Group G was registered before this change too, so the test passes even if `group_g4` were never wired into `_group_g_combined` (or if the combined wrapper were deleted and the old `group_g.run` registered directly). It validates nothing about the new registration.
  Suggestion: Assert that the registered "G" callable is the combined wrapper, or that a seeded G4 finding surfaces through `audit_detector` end-to-end (e.g., run the detector against the `_repo(..., None)` fixture and check a G4 finding appears).

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/triage_status_normalize.py:31-40 (`initial_record`)
  Finding: When the append line has no `id` key, `item_id` becomes the string `"None"` and is used both in the warning and the `_WARNED` dedupe key. Two different malformed records both missing ids collapse to one warning. Minor, but the message `append 'None'` is misleading.
  Suggestion: Guard with `isinstance(item.get("id"), str)` before warning/deduping, or surface the record's `ts`/`title` in the message instead.

- Category: regression
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/triage_cli.py:187-191
  Finding: `sp.add_argument("--project-root", ...)` is added unconditionally to every subparser. If any existing subcommand (e.g., `amend`, or a future `list` variant) already defines `--project-root`, argparse raises `ArgumentError` at parser build time and the whole CLI dies. The tests only exercise `list`.
  Suggestion: Skip subparsers that already define the option (check `sp._option_string_actions`), or at least add a smoke test that builds the parser and parses one arg per subcommand.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/group_g4.py:36-42 (`_ID_FULL` / `_TOKEN_RE`)
  Finding: A partial close in the *middle* of a list silently truncates the token list: `"Closes trg-A, trg-B (first half)"` yields `[trg-A]` — trg-A is reported even though the commit author may have meant a mixed close. The spec only pins the list-*starts*-with-partial case, so this is a defined-but-undocumented gap; a commit like this produces a finding on A that the convention `Part of trg-X` was designed to avoid.
  Suggestion: Either document this behavior in the grammar note in `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md`, or, if a partial appears anywhere in a matched token group, drop the whole group (consistent with the conservative starts-with-partial rule).

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/group_g4.py:110-118 (`_check` shallow check)
  Finding: `git_log_scan._run_git(...).strip()` will raise `AttributeError` if `_run_git` returns bytes on any code path; the surrounding `except Exception: pass` swallows it silently, so the shallow-clone annotation is lost rather than the spec's "a shallow clone is named in the detail". Swallowing is safe for findings but hides the lost annotation.
  Suggestion: Degrade explicitly (`except Exception: scope += ", shallow-clone check unavailable"` or log) so the known-limit annotation failure is visible.

Verified non-issues worth noting: the regex genuinely returns `[]` for a list starting with a partial id (the lookahead kills the first id and no restart point exists after the verb); the SUPPRESS-default subparser trick correctly preserves the pre-verb value and lets the post-verb value win (AC2 fully covered, including both-given and cwd-default); the GC resolver and reader now share `initial_record` so AC3's agreement is structural, not incidental; the changed `test_triage_expected_status.py` test would fail under the old behavior (`mark_status` previously raised `StatusPreconditionError`), so it's a real behavioral test.

Overall: the three ACs are implemented and mostly pinned by tests that fail on regressions; findings are refinements. Ship-with-fixes at most — the registry test is the one I'd insist on.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
